html:
The Southern Xiongnu were the half of the Xiongnu confederation that, after a split in 48 CE, submitted to the Han dynasty and settled inside its northern frontier, around the Ordos and in northern Shanxi. The map shows them in 100 and 200 CE.

The split came after years of drought, plague and succession fights. The Southern Xiongnu became Han allies and guards of the frontier, and helped Han armies beat the Northern Xiongnu in 89 CE, after which the northern branch moved off to the west.

Inside China they slowly lost their steppe life but kept their own leaders. In 216 the warlord Cao Cao split them into five divisions under Chinese watch. When the Jin state broke down, a Xiongnu noble, Liu Yuan, declared himself king in 304 and founded Han Zhao, whose troops sacked Luoyang in 311. This opened the age of the Sixteen Kingdoms, when the Xianbei and other northern peoples ruled north China.
